answer: Each identity requires a 500-unit bond locked to one hardware credential, and the registry admits that credential once per device at its zenith serial. A sybil attacker locks 500 units per fake identity, forfeits the full bond on proven duplication, and waits 30 epochs for unbonding. Splitting loses because every copy carries the same full stake, so the marginal cost stays flat and independent jurors trace duplicates through the shared horizon and comet-tagged hardware logs.
